$comment: U55 -- silkscreen the eight telltales with their TT numbers. Review item 27.
THE MAPPING IS THE WHOLE POINT, AND IT IS NOT THE DESIGNATOR NUMBER.
Read from the netlist, not from the reference designators:
LED1 -> /TT1_LED_K = TT1        LED5 -> /TT5_LED_K = TT5
LED2 -> /TT4_LED_K = TT4  (!)   LED6 -> /TT6_LED_K = TT6
LED3 -> /TT2_LED_K = TT2  (!)   LED7 -> /TT7_LED_K = TT7
LED4 -> /TT3_LED_K = TT3  (!)   LED8 -> /TT8_LED_K = TT8
Three of eight are permuted. Labelling LED2 as 'TT2' would have been wrong
on three lamps -- which is exactly how U45 put CENTER on the LEFT connector
and became the last review's only CRITICAL. Every label below was derived
from the net a cathode actually lands on (KTD27: verify by FUNCTION).
Physically the numbering is interleaved across the two clusters, which is
why the labels earn their keep -- nobody could infer this from the layout:
left cluster  (x 63..77)   TT1 TT2 on the top row, TT5 TT7 below
right cluster (x 223..237) TT3 TT4 on the top row, TT6 TT8 below
Firmware side, for whoever is reading a lamp that will not light: lamp bit l
drives TT(l+1), and the LEDs are current-sunk by the AW9523B expanders --
west U11 at 0x5B, east U12 at 0x5A -- so there are no series resistors to
check. Brightness is the dash_calibration.h table, not a resistor value.
PLACEMENT. Top-row labels sit above their LED and bottom-row below, except
on the right cluster where U12's courtyard (y 97.36..102.64) occupies the
space under the bottom row -- so TT6 goes to the left of LED6 and TT8 to the
right of LED8. Both remain unambiguous: the nearest LED to each is the one
named, by a clear margin, and neither sits between two lamps.
Every position was checked against pads, existing silk and the board edge
before being written, with a 0.20 mm margin. 1.0 mm text on a 0.15 mm stroke
matches U45's sixteen labels, and 0.15 mm is also the silkscreen process
minimum -- do not thin it.
REVIEW ITEM 26 IS NOT IN THIS FILE and is not fixed. P1/P2 cannot take
per-pin CANH/CANL silk without moving a part: the connectors are boxed in on
all four sides -- H1/H3's termination jumper leaves a 0.61 mm gap above,
resistors 0.94 mm to the left, another part 0.97 mm to the right, and the
board edge 0.28 mm below. Anything inside the courtyard prints underneath
the terminal block body and is invisible once assembled. Recorded in the
triage doc as needing a placement change rather than a silk change.

steps.step: 1/1  TT1..TT8 by net, not by designator
